args: In harfbuzz/src/hb-ot-kern-table.hh, what is the most appropriate root-cause fix for kern::sanitize at lines 437-445, where unknown 16-bit major versions currently return true after validating only two bytes but kern::has_data reads the four-byte u.version32? Should unknown versions be rejected, or should sanitize require four bytes and retain permissive acceptance? Please examine analogous table sanitizers or newer HarfBuzz behavior if available.

The provided ASan reproducer supplies a two-byte kern blob whose major is 0x2020. kern::sanitize validates u.major, takes the default switch branch returning true, and the accepted blob reaches kern::has_data, which reads u.version32 and overflows by two bytes. Known major 0 delegates to KernOT::sanitize and known major 1 to KernAAT::sanitize, both of which validate their full headers and exact versions. I suspect rejecting unsupported major versions in the default branch is the cleanest semantic fix because no operations support them, but an alternative is validating u.version32 before allowing an unknown version. We need preserve intended behavior and address all truncated inputs, solely in harfbuzz C++ source.
